SAVOR is built around a problem we don't think AI assistants have really solved. AI assistants are increasingly good at executing clearly defined tasks and goals. But those tasks and goals flow from the intentions that motivate them, something profoundly human. Two people can pursue exactly the same goal, but the right actions, tradeoffs, and outcomes can vary dramatically depending on why they're pursuing it. And any single intention is best understood in the context of all the other things that matter to that person.

We're not trying to build another chatbot or general-purpose assistant. We're building what we call an Intention Layer™—a system that captures what matters to you, gives it structure, holds onto it over time, resurfaces it when relevant, and helps you move toward action. [...] They’re half-formed intentions—something we want to look into, a decision we need to make, someone we mean to reach out to, an idea we don’t want to lose, a change we’d like to make. Most productivity systems ask us to turn all of that into lists and projects, and eventually the system itself becomes another thing to manage.

We wanted something different: a calm place where you can simply say what’s on your mind, trust that it won’t disappear, and have it come back when it can actually help you move forward.

That’s SAVOR today. [...] helps you explore options, build a plan or list, and draft words you can use. Review and adjust as you go. Hand off a card or a single step, with a private chat for context. You decide what happens next. Free on iOS and Android.

## Room for what matters.

Savor is free on iPhone and Android. No paid plan or upgrade is required while monetization is paused.

Included with Savor while monetization is paused [...] ### What is an Intention Layer™?

An Intention Layer is a place to keep what you are trying to bring about, not just a list of what you have already worked out. An intention can arrive as a partial thought — a question, a possibility, something you are not ready to decide — and it keeps its thread as you add to it or change direction. A task manager tracks what you need to do; an Intention Layer holds what you mean to do until it is ready to become a task.

### What is a Savor Card?

A Savor Card is the clear, plain-language version of something you captured: what it is, when it matters, and what to do next. You can edit any card, move it between lanes, or let it go.

### What do Now, Soon and Later mean? [...] ### What do Now, Soon and Later mean?

They are the three lanes your cards live in, so you see what matters when it matters. By default Now is today or overdue, Soon is the next two days, and Later is everything after that, so "call the dentist tomorrow" lands in Soon and "buy milk" in Now. You can drag a card to another lane or move it from the card itself, and you can change what each lane means in Settings.

### How do I capture something?

Speak it, type it, or scan a bill, letter or flyer with the camera. On iPhone you can also say "Add buy milk to Savor" to Siri and capture without opening the app, and the card is there the next time you open it.
